title: Understanding One-hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a method to represent categorical data as binary vectors. Each category is represented by a vector with a single high (1) bit and all other bits low (0).

title: How Many Codons?
text: Each DNA string is composed of 3,000 letters. Since a codon is a sequence of $$3$$ letters, how many codons are there in a single DNA string?

title: Possible Codons
text: There are $$4$$ possible letters (T, G, C, A) and each codon is a sequence of $$3$$ letters. How many possible codons can be formed?

title: Calculate Possible Codons

title: One-hot Encoding Dimensions
text: To find the number of dimensions for one-hot encoding, multiply the number of codons in a DNA string by the number of possible codons.
